# fivenines_proxmox_guests (Data Source)

The VMs and containers on the Proxmox cluster this instance reports -- which guest is stopped and since when, and which node currently holds it.

THESE ROWS ARE NOT THIS INSTANCE'S. Proxmox inventory is CLUSTER-scoped and organization-owned, and only the cluster's authoritative reporter writes it, so every instance reporting a cluster returns the SAME rows with the same ids. The data source is nested under an instance because that is how a caller REACHES the cluster. Deduplicate on `id` if you read more than one instance in a cluster.

AN INSTANCE WHOSE REPORTER HAS AGED OUT RETURNS AN EMPTY LIST, not the cluster's last known rows. `collector.enabled` stays true in that case, so an empty list there is about reporter freshness rather than configuration.

A GUEST MIGRATES: `vmid` is unique cluster-wide and the row is keyed on cluster + vmid, so `node_name` is where the guest lives right now, not a stable attribute of it. `stale` here is the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold, matching what every guest trigger reads -- NOT the fixed ten minutes the nodes and storages data sources use.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# These rows are the CLUSTER's, not this instance's: every instance reporting
# the cluster returns the same rows with the same ids. Deduplicate on id if you
# read more than one instance in a cluster.
data "fivenines_proxmox_guests" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.pve_reporter.id
}

output "stopped_guests" {
  value = [
    for g in data.fivenines_proxmox_guests.all.proxmox_guests :
    "${g.guest_type}/${g.vmid}" if g.status == "stopped"
  ]
}

# A guest migrates, so node_name is where it lives right now rather than a
# stable attribute of it. Stale rows are listed and flagged, never hidden.
output "guest_placement" {
  value = {
    for g in data.fivenines_proxmox_guests.all.proxmox_guests :
    g.vmid => ({ node = g.node_name, stale = g.stale })
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `guest_type` (String) Filter by guest kind. One of: `vm`, `lxc`.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the guest name or vmid.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter, built on the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold here -- matching what every guest trigger reads, and NOT the fixed ten minutes the nodes and storages data sources use. Omit for both.
- `status` (String) Filter by guest state. One of: `unknown`, `stopped`, `running`, `paused`, `suspended`.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `proxmox_guests` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--proxmox_guests))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--proxmox_guests"></a>
### Nested Schema for `proxmox_guests`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `guest_type` (String) A full VM or an LXC container -- genuinely different things behind one Proxmox API. One of: `vm`, `lxc`.
- `id` (String) Row identifier.
- `last_synced_at` (String) Server arrival time of the tick that last refreshed this row (never the agent's clock). Null when the row has never synced.
- `name` (String) The guest name as Proxmox reports it. Null when unnamed; `vmid` is the identity.
- `node_name` (String) The hosting node's name, denormalized so a row is legible without a second call. Null only if the node row went missing.
- `proxmox_cluster_id` (String) The cluster these rows belong to. NOT the instance: Proxmox inventory is cluster-scoped, so every instance reporting this cluster returns the same rows with the same ids. Deduplicate on `id` if you poll more than one.
- `proxmox_node_id` (String) The node currently hosting the guest. Changes on migration.
- `stale` (Boolean) Measured against the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold, matching what every guest trigger, the fleet grid and the workflow engine read. This is a DIFFERENT window from the one ProxmoxNode and ProxmoxStorage use (a fixed ten minutes), so the same age can read stale here and fresh there. The divergence is the product's, and the endpoints reproduce it rather than agreeing with each other at the cost of agreeing with the alerts.
- `state_changed_at` (String) When `status` last changed -- the field that turns "it is stopped" into "it has been stopped since 04:10", and the one the guest-status trigger reads.
- `status` (String) `unknown` is a real value: it is what an unrecognized Proxmox state maps to, and means "we could not classify it", not "the guest is gone". One of: `unknown`, `stopped`, `running`, `paused`, `suspended`.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
- `vmid` (String) The Proxmox id an operator recognizes ("VM 1042"). A STRING, because that is how Proxmox reports it and how the row is keyed.
